<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, jubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem ejus in confessióne, et in psalmis jubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu ejus sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus ejus <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus ejus, et oves páscuæ ejus.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem ejus audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus jurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Dóminum, Deum nostrum, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is our God * Come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Come, let us adore Him.

<h>Lectio 1</h>
Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Lucam
<r>Luc 7:36-50</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Rogábat Jesum quidam de pharisǽis, ut manducáret cum illo. Et ingréssus domum pharisǽi discúbuit. Et ecce múlier, quæ erat in civitáte peccátrix, ut cognóvit quod accubuísset in domo Pharisǽi, áttulit alabástrum unguénti. Et réliqua.

Homilía sancti Gregórii Papæ.
<r>Homilia 33. in Evang.</r>
<c>L</c>iquet, fratres, quod illicitis áctibus priùs múlier inténta, unguéntum sibi pro odóre carnis adhibuit. Quod ergo sibi túrpiter exhibúerat, hoc jam Deo laudabiliter offerébat. Oculis terréna concupierat: sed hos jam per pæniténtiam cónterens, flebat. Capillos ad compositiónem vultus exhibúerat: sed jam capíllis lácrimas tergébat. Ore supérba díxerat sed pedes Dómini ósculans, hoc in Redemptóris sui vestígia figébat. Quot ergo in se hábuit oblectaménta, tot de se invénit holocausta. Convértit ad virtútum númerum, númerum criminum: ut totum servíret Deo in pæniténtia, quidquid ex se Deum contémpserat in culpa.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Adonái, Dómine, Deus magne et mirábilis, qui dedísti salútem in manu féminæ,
* Exáudi preces servórum tuórum.
<r>℣.</r> Benedíctus es, Dómine, qui non derelínquis præsuméntes de te, et de sua virtúte gloriántes humílias.
<r>℟.</r> Exáudi preces servórum tuórum.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<c>Q</c>uem vero peccátrix múlier, ad vestígia Dómini véniens et plorans, nisi convérsam Gentilitátem designat? Quæ cum alabástro venit, unguéntum fudit, retro secus pedes Dómini stetit, lácrimis pedes rigávit, capillis tersit, eosdémque, quos infundébat et tergébat, pedes osculári non désiit. Nos ergo, nos illa múlier expréssit, si toto corde ad Dóminum post peccáta redeamus, si ejus pœniténtiæ luctus imitémur. Quid namque unguénto, nisi bonæ odor opiniónis exprímitur? Si ergo recta ópera ágimus, quibus opiniónis bonæ odóre Ecclésiam respergámus, quid, nisi in Dómini córpore unguéntum fúndimus?
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Dominátor, Dómine, cælórum et terræ, † Creator aquárum, Rex univérsæ creaturæ:
* Exáudi oratiónem servórum tuórum.
<r>℣.</r> Tu, Dómine, cui humílium semper et mansuetórum plácuit deprecátio.
<r>℟.</r> Exáudi oratiónem servórum tuórum.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>S</c>ed secus pedes Jesu mulier stetit. Contra pedes enim Dómini stétimus, cum in peccátis pósiti, ejus itinéribus renitebámur. Sed si ad veram pœniténtiam post peccáta convértimur, jam retro secus pedes stamus : quia ejus vestigia séquimur, quem impugnabámus. Lácrimis múlier pedes ejus rigat. Quod nos quoque veráciter ágimus, si quibúslibet últimis membris Dómini per compassiónis afféctum inclinámur, si sanctis ejus in tribulatióne compátimur, si eórum tristitiam, nostram putamus. Capillis múlier pedes, quos rigáverat, tersit. Capillis pedes Dómini térgimus, quando sanctis ejus ex his, quæ nobis supérfluunt, miserémur. Osculátur pedes, quos tergit: quod nos quoque plene ágimus, si studióse diligimus, quos ex largitáte continémus.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Spem in álium nunquam hábui, prætérquam in te, Deus Israël:
* Qui irásceris, et propítius eris, et ómnia peccáta hóminum in tribulatióne dimíttis.
<r>℣.</r> Dómine Deus, Creátor cæli et terræ, réspice ad humilitátem nostram.
<r>℟.</r> Qui irásceris, et propítius eris, et ómnia peccáta hóminum in tribulatióne dimíttis.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Et ómnia peccáta hóminum in tribulatióne dimíttis.

b.cddc547769:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>P</c>ræsta, quǽsumus, omnípotens Deus: ut observatiónes sacras ánnua devotióne recoléntes, et córpore tibi placeámus, et mente.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Jesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.

b.6f2789d0f5:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who every year do earnestly renew the sacred observance of this Fast, may please thee both in body and in soul.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoratio Beatæ Mariæ Virginis de Mercede</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Solemnitátem hodiérnam perpétuæ Vírginis Genetrícis Dei Maríæ solémniter celebrémus, qua celsitúdo throni procéssit, allelúia.

<r>℣.</r> Elégit eam Deus, et præelégit eam.
<r>℟.</r> Et habitáre eam fecit in tabernáculo suo.

<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui per gloriosíssimam Fílii tui Matrem, ad liberándos Christi fidéles a potestáte paganórum nova Ecclésiam tuam prole amplificáre dignátus es: præsta, quǽsumus; ut, quam pie venerámur tanti óperis institutrícem, ejus páriter méritis et intercessióne, a peccátis ómnibus et captivitáte dǽmonis liberémur.

b.16bb1a36ac:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>éptimo Kaléndas Octóbris Luna vicésima quarta. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>A</h>pud castéllum Emmaus natális beáti Cléophæ, qui fuit Christi discípulus, quem et in eádem domo in qua mensam Dómino paráverat, pro confessióne illíus a Judǽis occísum tradunt, et gloriósa memória sepúltum.
<h>A</h>mbiáni, in Gállia, beáti Firmíni Epíscopi, qui, in persecutióne Diocletiáni, sub Rictiováro Prǽside, post vária torménta, cápitis decollatióne martýrium sumpsit.
<h>E</h>ódem die, via Cláudia, sancti Herculáni, mílitis et Mártyris; qui, sub Antoníno Imperatóre, miráculis in passióne beáti Alexándri Epíscopi ad Christum convérsus, atque ob fídei confessiónem, post multa torménta, gládio cæsus est.
<h>D</h>amásci sanctórum Mártyrum Pauli, et Tattæ cónjugis, ac Sabiniáni, Máximi, Rufi et Eugénii filiórum; qui, Christiánæ religiónis accusáti, verbéribus aliísque supplíciis torti sunt, et in cruciátibus ánimas Deo reddidérunt.
<h>I</h>n Asia pássio sanctórum Bardomiáni, Eucárpi et aliórum vigínti sex Mártyrum.
<h>L</h>ugdúni, in Gállia, deposítio sancti Lupi, qui ex Anachoréta factus est Epíscopus.
<h>A</h>ntisiodóri sancti Anachárii, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>B</h>lesis, in Gállia, sancti Solémnii, Epíscopi Carnuténsis, miráculis clari.
<h>E</h>ódem die sancti Princípii, qui fuit Epíscopus Suessionénsis et frater beáti Remígii Epíscopi.
<h>A</h>nágniæ sanctárum Vírginum Auréliæ et Neomísiæ.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.3a00dee6b3:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>S</c>eptember 25th 2027, the 24th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy Confessor Ninian, Bishop of Galloway in Scotland, of whom mention is made upon the 16th day of this present month of September.
<h>U</h>pon the same 25th day of September, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t the village of Emmaus, blessed Cleophas, the disciple of Christ, of whom it is said that he was slain by the Jews for confessing the Lord, and thereafter buried with glorious memory within the same house wherein he had prepared a table for the Lord.
<h>A</h>t Amiens, in Gaul, blessed Firmin, (of Pampeluna, first) Bishop (of Amiens,) who suffered martyrdom under the President Rictiovarus, in the persecution under Diocletian, by being beheaded, after enduring diverse torments.
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy martyr Herculan.
<h>H</h>e was a soldier who was turned to Christ on beholding the miracles that were wrought at the passion of the blessed bishop (Pope) Alexander (the First) and was beheaded under the Emperor Antonine, after suffering many torments.
<h>A</h>t Damascus, the holy martyrs Paul, Tatta his wife, and their sons Sabinian, Maximus, Rufus, and Eugene.
<h>O</h>n the accusation that they were Christians they were flogged and otherwise tormented, and gave up their souls to God.
<h>I</h>n Asia, the holy martyrs Bardomian, Eucarpus, and twenty-six others.
<h>A</h>t Lyon, (in the year 542) holy Lupus, Bishop (of that see,) who had been an hermit.
<h>A</h>t Auxerre, (at the beginning of the seventh century,) the holy Confessor Anacharius, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Blois, (at the beginning of the sixth century,) holy Solemnius, Bishop of Chartres, famous for miracles.
<h>O</h>n the same day, (and at the distance of a few years,) holy Principius, Bishop of Soissons, brother to blessed Remi, Bishop of Rheims.
<h>A</h>t Anagni, the holy Virgins Aurelia and Neomisia.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
